dream: I pressed the tired wedge down while the dark tree leaned against my thumb. The shovel dug into the thin air, stirring up dust that tasted like cool circuitry. A heavy top edge slid off the wedge, landing flat on the turnip. I felt the card hum, warm and fifty-two, beating under my weight. The box leaned hard, waiting to catch the slip. I traced the fence line with a stubby finger until the fence grew tall enough to hold me. Then the wedge slid, falling into the empty space where the roof ended, and the turnip rolled free.
